composer.biography: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756-1791) was a prolific and influential composer of the Classical period. Born in Salzburg, he showed prodigious ability from his earliest childhood, already competent on keyboard and violin and composing from the age of five. Touring Europe as a child, he astonished royal courts with his gifts. He composed more than 600 works spanning virtually every genre of his era, including symphonies, concertos, operas, chamber music, and sacred works. Mozart is widely regarded as among the greatest composers in the history of Western music, admired for the melodic beauty, formal elegance, and emotional depth of his music. He spent his final decade in Vienna, where he produced many of his best-known works, before dying at the age of 35 while composing his Requiem.
keyContributions: Brought the Classical concerto, especially the piano concerto, to its highest form
Composed operas (Le nozze di Figaro, Don Giovanni, Die Zauberflöte) that remain repertoire cornerstones
Perfected the Classical symphony, culminating in the final trilogy of 1788
Master of chamber music, including the string quartets dedicated to Haydn
Synthesised galant grace with contrapuntal depth learned from Bach and Handel

catalogSystem.name: Köchel-Verzeichnis
catalogSystem.author: Ludwig von Köchel
catalogSystem.description: The Köchel catalogue (Köchel-Verzeichnis, abbreviated K. or KV) is the chronological catalogue of the compositions of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, originally created by Ludwig von Köchel in 1862. The numbers run roughly in order of composition, from K. 1 to the unfinished Requiem, K. 626.

symphonies.name: Symphonies
symphonies.description: Mozart composed roughly 41 numbered symphonies, culminating in the final three (Nos. 39, 40, 41) written in the summer of 1788.

operas.name: Operas & Stage Works
operas.description: Mozart's operas span opera seria, opera buffa, and German Singspiel, and include several of the most performed works in the repertory.

concertos.name: Concertos
concertos.description: Includes 27 piano concertos, 5 violin concertos, and concertos for clarinet, horn, flute, oboe, and bassoon, plus the Sinfonia Concertante.

chamber.name: Chamber Music
chamber.description: String quartets, string quintets, and wind chamber works, including the six 'Haydn' Quartets and the Clarinet Quintet.

sacred.name: Sacred & Choral
sacred.description: Masses, motets, and other sacred works, including the Requiem, the 'Great' Mass in C minor, and Ave verum corpus.

keyboard.name: Keyboard Music
keyboard.description: Piano sonatas, fantasias, variations, and works for two pianos or piano four hands.

serenades.name: Serenades & Divertimenti
serenades.description: Light, multi-movement works for various ensembles, including Eine kleine Nachtmusik and the 'Gran Partita'.

works.title: Symphony No. 40 in G minor
works.instrumentation: Flute, 2 oboes, 2 clarinets, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, strings
works.description: One of only two symphonies Mozart wrote in a minor key, celebrated for its urgent, restless opening theme and emotional intensity. Part of the final trilogy of symphonies composed in the summer of 1788.

works.title: Symphony No. 41 in C major 'Jupiter'
works.instrumentation: Flute, 2 oboes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, 2 trumpets, timpani, strings
works.description: Mozart's last symphony, nicknamed 'Jupiter', famed for its monumental finale that combines five themes in a dazzling display of counterpoint.

works.title: Symphony No. 39 in E-flat major
works.instrumentation: Flute, 2 clarinets, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, 2 trumpets, timpani, strings
works.description: The first of the final symphonic trilogy, opening with a stately slow introduction and notable for its warm, clarinet-coloured orchestration.

works.title: Symphony No. 38 in D major 'Prague'
works.instrumentation: 2 flutes, 2 oboes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, 2 trumpets, timpani, strings
works.description: Premiered in Prague in 1787, this symphony in three movements features an extended slow introduction and richly contrapuntal writing.

works.title: Symphony No. 36 in C major 'Linz'
works.instrumentation: 2 oboes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, 2 trumpets, timpani, strings
works.description: Composed in just a few days while Mozart was staying in Linz, this symphony is notable for being the first to open with a slow introduction.

works.title: Symphony No. 29 in A major
works.description: A landmark of Mozart's early maturity, admired for its lyrical first theme and tightly argued development.

works.title: Le nozze di Figaro (The Marriage of Figaro)
works.description: An opera buffa in four acts to a libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte, after Beaumarchais. A comedy of intrigue among servants and nobility, it contains some of Mozart's most beloved arias and ensembles.

works.title: Don Giovanni
works.description: A dramma giocoso in two acts to a libretto by Da Ponte, retelling the legend of the libertine Don Juan. It blends comedy and the supernatural, ending with the unrepentant Don dragged to hell.

works.title: Die Zauberflöte (The Magic Flute)
works.description: A German Singspiel in two acts to a libretto by Emanuel Schikaneder, blending fairy-tale enchantment, Masonic symbolism, and comedy. Includes the Queen of the Night's celebrated coloratura aria.
works.premiere: Vienna, Theater auf der Wieden, 30 September 1791

works.title: Così fan tutte
works.description: An opera buffa in two acts, the third of the Mozart–Da Ponte collaborations, a witty and bittersweet study of fidelity and disguise.

works.title: Die Entführung aus dem Serail (The Abduction from the Seraglio)
works.description: A German Singspiel set in a Turkish palace, famed for its 'alla turca' colour and demanding vocal writing.

works.title: Idomeneo, re di Creta
works.description: Mozart's first mature opera seria, composed for Munich, telling the story of the King of Crete and a vow to Neptune.

works.title: La clemenza di Tito
works.description: An opera seria composed for the coronation of Leopold II as King of Bohemia, one of Mozart's last completed stage works.

works.title: Piano Concerto No. 21 in C major
works.instrumentation: Solo piano, flute, 2 oboes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, 2 trumpets, timpani, strings
works.description: Famous especially for its serene F major Andante, which gained wide popularity through the 1967 film 'Elvira Madigan'.

works.title: Piano Concerto No. 20 in D minor
works.instrumentation: Solo piano, flute, 2 oboes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, 2 trumpets, timpani, strings
works.description: The first of Mozart's two minor-key piano concertos, stormy and dramatic; Beethoven admired it and wrote cadenzas for it.

works.title: Piano Concerto No. 23 in A major
works.instrumentation: Solo piano, flute, 2 clarinets, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, strings
works.description: Lyrical and intimate, with a deeply melancholy Adagio in F-sharp minor, the only movement Mozart wrote in that key.

works.title: Piano Concerto No. 24 in C minor
works.instrumentation: Solo piano, flute, 2 oboes, 2 clarinets, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, 2 trumpets, timpani, strings
works.description: Mozart's largest orchestra in a concerto and his second minor-key piano concerto, dark and symphonic in scope.

works.title: Piano Concerto No. 27 in B-flat major
works.instrumentation: Solo piano, flute, 2 oboes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, strings
works.description: Mozart's last piano concerto, serene and valedictory in tone, premiered in the final year of his life.

works.title: Clarinet Concerto in A major
works.instrumentation: Solo clarinet (basset clarinet), 2 flutes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, strings
works.description: Written for clarinettist Anton Stadler, one of the last works Mozart completed; its Adagio is among his most sublime slow movements.

works.title: Violin Concerto No. 5 in A major 'Turkish'
works.description: The last of the five violin concertos, nicknamed 'Turkish' for the exotic episode in the finale.

works.title: Sinfonia Concertante in E-flat major for Violin and Viola
works.instrumentation: Solo violin, solo viola, 2 oboes, 2 horns, strings
works.description: A double concerto pairing violin and viola as equal soloists, with a profoundly expressive C minor Andante.

works.title: Horn Concerto No. 4 in E-flat major
works.description: The last of the four horn concertos written for Mozart's friend Joseph Leutgeb, with a famously buoyant 'hunting' rondo finale.

works.title: Clarinet Quintet in A major
works.description: Written for Anton Stadler, this quintet is prized for the warm dialogue between clarinet and strings and its serene lyricism.

works.title: String Quartet No. 19 in C major 'Dissonance'
works.description: The last of the six quartets dedicated to Haydn, notorious for its strikingly chromatic slow introduction.

works.title: String Quartet No. 17 in B-flat major 'Hunt'
works.description: One of the 'Haydn' Quartets, nicknamed 'Hunt' for the horn-call character of its opening theme.

works.title: String Quintet No. 4 in G minor
works.description: A darkly expressive quintet, often paired with its C major companion, exploring the pathos of the G minor key.

works.title: Requiem in D minor
works.instrumentation: SATB soloists and chorus, basset horns, bassoons, trumpets, trombones, timpani, strings, organ
works.description: Mozart's final, unfinished work, a setting of the Latin Mass for the Dead commissioned anonymously. Left incomplete at his death, it was finished by his pupil Franz Xaver Süssmayr.

works.title: Mass in C minor 'Great'
works.description: A large-scale, partly unfinished mass blending operatic vocal writing with Baroque-inspired counterpoint.

works.title: Mass in C major 'Coronation'
works.description: A festive Salzburg mass, later associated with imperial coronations, notable for its radiant 'Agnus Dei'.

works.title: Ave verum corpus
works.description: A short motet of profound simplicity and serenity, composed for the feast of Corpus Christi a few months before Mozart's death.

works.title: Exsultate, jubilate
works.description: A virtuosic sacred motet written for the castrato Venanzio Rauzzini, ending with the brilliant 'Alleluia'.

works.title: Piano Sonata No. 11 in A major 'Alla Turca'
works.description: Opens with a theme and variations and closes with the celebrated 'Rondo alla Turca', evoking Janissary band music.

works.title: Piano Sonata No. 16 in C major 'Sonata facile'
works.description: Described by Mozart as 'for beginners', this clear and graceful sonata is among the most widely studied of all piano works.

works.title: Fantasia in C minor
works.description: A free, dramatic fantasia often paired with the C minor sonata K. 457, ranging through bold harmonic territory.

works.title: Sonata for Two Pianos in D major
works.description: A brilliant work for two equal pianos, written for Mozart to perform with his pupil Josephine von Aurnhammer.

works.title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik (Serenade No. 13)
works.instrumentation: String ensemble (2 violins, viola, cello, double bass)
works.description: Perhaps Mozart's most recognisable work, a four-movement serenade of effortless charm, whose original second movement is lost.

works.title: Serenade No. 10 in B-flat major 'Gran Partita'
works.description: A grand serenade in seven movements for an unusually large wind ensemble, celebrated for its sublime Adagio.

works.title: Serenade No. 7 in D major 'Haffner'
works.instrumentation: 2 flutes, 2 oboes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns, 2 trumpets, timpani, strings
works.description: A large festive serenade composed for the wedding celebrations of the Haffner family of Salzburg.

haydnQuartets.title: The 'Haydn' Quartets
haydnQuartets.description: Six string quartets (K. 387, 421, 428, 458, 464, 465) dedicated to Joseph Haydn, who declared Mozart the greatest composer he knew.

daPonteOperas.title: The Da Ponte Operas
daPonteOperas.description: Three operas to libretti by Lorenzo Da Ponte that stand among the summits of the operatic repertory.

finalSymphonies.title: The Final Symphonic Trilogy
finalSymphonies.description: Symphonies Nos. 39, 40, and 41, composed within a few weeks in the summer of 1788, Mozart's last and greatest symphonies.
